usage: Shukran is the standard, universally understood word for thank you across the Levant, suitable for both formal and casual situations. In everyday interactions, Levantine speakers frequently use yeslamo (literally may your hands be safe) when receiving something physical, or ya3teek el 3afye (may God give you health) to acknowledge someone's effort.

variants.label: to a man
variants.note: Adds a personal pronoun to make the thanks more direct to a male listener.

variants.label: to a woman
variants.note: Adds a personal pronoun to make the thanks more direct to a female listener.

variants.label: when handed something
variants.note: Extremely common in the Levant when someone physically hands you an object, like food or a cup of coffee.

variants.label: for someone's effort
variants.note: Used to thank service workers, colleagues, or anyone who has performed a task for you.

responses.english: and your hands (standard response to yeslamo, when speaking to a man)

examples.english: Thank you very much for your help.
Thank you, we troubled you with us.
